checks.rule: Estate plans must clearly show scale and orientation and be drawn to the quoted scale.
The preferred scale is 1:500, with 1:1250 potentially satisfactory when layout and boundaries remain clear.
Plans marked 'For Identification only' or 'Do not scale from this drawing' are not acceptable for this specification.
The plan must be based on an accurate survey plotted to the chosen scale.
Survey accuracy should be within 0.3 mm at map scale plus one part in one thousand of measured distance.
Survey control stations should preserve the datum used for the original survey through setting-out and as-built work.
Measurements must be shown in metric form.
External plot boundaries should be precisely defined to avoid misinterpretation.
Require scale, orientation and datum provenance before treating a development survey as high-precision boundary evidence.
Reject PDF-derived scale measurements if print scaling is not verified.
Where survey and OS mapping materially differ, preserve the discrepancy instead of snapping one source to the other.
Promote survey-derived candidate geometry only when its stated tolerance is compatible with the requested elevation precision.
